claim: A hand-optimized exact 4-bit multiplier can be implemented on Xilinx 7-series FPGAs using only 11 LUTs and 2 CARRY4 blocks, one LUT fewer than the prior best 12-LUT design.
stance_target: small FPGA arithmetic-circuit projects can achieve genuine, publishable novelty via LUT-level redesign
scope_conditions: AMD Xilinx 7-series FPGA (Artix-7 35T, Arty A7 board), Vivado 2024.2, area-optimized synthesis
quoted_support: This paper proposes a hardware-efficient accurate 4-bit multiplier design for AMD Xilinx 7-series FPGAs using only 11 LUTs and two CARRY4 blocks... Evaluation confirms that the circuit attains minimal resource usage and a critical-path delay of 2.750 ns.

claim: Standard RTL multiplication (a*b) synthesized directly in Vivado 2024.2 does not produce the resource-minimal LUT mapping; manual/structural HDL design is required to reach the optimum.
stance_target: manual logic design (not just behavioral Verilog) is a viable novelty axis for undergraduate FPGA papers
quoted_support: in Xilinx's Vivado 2024.2 toolchain, an RTL description written simply as a product (e.g., p = a*b) does not infer our proposed structure. A central contribution of this work is to show that a carefully manually designed 4-bit multiplier achieves higher performance than the automatically synthesized counterpart.

claim: Comparison table shows the proposed 11-LUT/2-CARRY4 design has the lowest resource usage among 8 compared multiplier designs while ranking second-lowest in critical-path delay (2.750 ns), only slightly behind an Exact/PerfOpt design that uses far more LUTs.
stance_target: resource-vs-delay tradeoff comparison tables are a standard, reproducible evaluation format for FPGA arithmetic papers
quoted_support: the proposed multiplier con- sists of 11 LUTs and 2 CARRY4 units, exhibiting the low- est resource usage compared to other multipliers. Regard- ing delay, the critical path delay of the proposed multiplier is 2.750 ns, the second smallest after both Exact config- urations.

claim: Algebraic simplification of carry-dominance logic (C1 = A1B2*A2B1 replacing a longer OR-of-AND expression) is the specific mechanism enabling the 1-LUT reduction.
stance_target: small, well-documented Boolean simplifications constitute legitimate, presentable novelty in a short conference paper
scope_conditions: carry computation for 4-bit partial-product addition in the S1 column
quoted_support: By observing logical dominance, this can be simplified to C1 = A1B2 * A2B1, thereby reducing the number of required signals and, in turn, the number of LUTs.
